context_before.text: The weldment performance was investigated on the toughness and the pitting resistance at their heat affected zone(HAZ). The welded joints were produced employing multipass gas tungsten arc welding(GTAW) with the welding conditions shown in Fig. 1. The toughness was evaluated by the Charpy impact test at 273K(0°C) using a specimen with a V notch at the position 2mm distant from the fusion line where the absorbed energy was most decreased. The pitting corrosion resistance was evaluated by the pitting potential(Vc') of the simulated HAZ specimen which was affected by the thermal cycle with the peak temperature of 1648K(1375°C) shown in Fig. 2.The pitting potential was measured by the potential sweep method at the rate of 20mV/min in synthetic seawater.at 353K(80°C)

Fig. 3 shows the effect of the Ni and N contents on the Charpy impact values of the weldment. The N content was found to make little influence on the toughness. The Ni content, on the other hand, remarkably affected the toughness. The impact value showed the maximum value at about 7% Ni. The mechanism of the toughness deterioration at the HAZ was clarified by transmission electron microscopic(TEM) observation [11l. It was caused by the Cr carbo-nitride precipitation in the lower Ni region and by the sigma phase precipitation in the higher Ni one. Fig. 4 shows the effect of N content on the pitting potential of the simulated HAZ of alloys containing 6 to 8%Ni. The pitting potential reached 0.6V with the 0.3%N addition. It was confirmed that the addition of N was beneficial to improve the pitting corrosion resistance as has been reported in references [12],[13].

context_after.text: The effect of Ni and N contents on the HAZ performance is summarized in Fig. 5. From the viewpoint of the HAZ performance the optimum contents of Ni and N were found to be 7% and 0.3%, respectively. Consequently, The principal composition of the super-duplex SS was decided to be 27.5%Cr-7%Ni-3.8%Mo-0.3%N.

The seamless tube of the 28%Cr duplex SS with the optimum chemical composition was manufactured through the P/M process shown in Fig. 6 [14]. The duplex SS powder was atomized by nitrogen gas and packed into a mild steel capsule. The powder billet was processed by cold isostatic pressing(CIP) and hot extruded to the tube. The tube was acid pickled in order to remove the capsule and then heat treated at 1373K(1100°C) followed by water quenching.

context_before.text: Crevice corrosion is more important problem than pitting corrosion for SSs because the former occurs more frequently than the latter in chloride containing environments such as seawater. The crevice corrosion potential of the all materials became less noble than the pitting potential at the same temperature.as shown in Fig. 8. The results obtained at 353K(80°C) gave the following rank on the crevice corrosion resistance: 25%Cr duplex SS < super-austenitic SS(254) < 28%Cr duplex SS < super-ferritic SS(2942) which indicates that the ferritic SS is more resistant to crevice corrosion than the austenitic one even with the same P. I. value in contrast to the.pitting corrosion resistance shown in Fig. 8 [5], [15]. Fig. 9 shows the effect of temperature and chloride concentration on the crevice corrosion behavior of the alloys by the constant potential test at 0.4V in NaCl solutions for 48h. The difference in the critical chloride concentration among the alloys was consistent with the rank obtained from the crevice corrosion potential in Fig. 8. The 28%Cr duplex SS and the super-ferritic SS were the most resistant to crevice corrosion. The 28%Cr duplex SS showed a good corrosion resistance in the immersion test for 6 months in the actual seawater; it suffered no crevice corrosion.

The corrosion resistance of the weldment is important for duplex SSs. It has been reported that the corrosion resistance of duplex SSs is deteriorated by the microstructure change and the precipitation of carbo-nitride and intermetallic compound at the weldment [11],[12],[16]. Fig. 10 shows the ferrite content and the pitting potential of the 25%Cr and the 28%Cr duplex SSs after heat treatment for 10s at various temperature. The ferrite content of the 25%Cr duplex SS increased with increasing temperature to reach about 80% after 1623K(1350°C) heating. The ferrite content of the 28%Cr duplex SS did not change so much; it was still only 65% after 1623K(1350°C) heating. That is attributed to the rapid austenite phase formation during the cooling on the 28%Cr duplex SS which contains high N of 0.3%. Nitrogen atom is the potential element for stabilizing the austenitic phase and diffuses more rapidly than the metal element atoms such as Ni, Cr and Mo. Although the pitting potentials of the both duplex SSs were decreased in the same manner, the 28%Cr duplex SS after 1623K(1350°C) heating was still more resistant to pitting corrosion than the 25%Cr duplex SS's base metal.

context_before.text: The corrosion resistance of the welded joint was investigated to clarify the effect of the welding procedure. Firstly, the girth welding was performed by GTAW with the heat input of 6 to 13.5kJ/cm using the similar filler metal to the 28%Cr duplex SS. The results are shown in Fig. 11 where the pitting potential is plotted against the heat input. The pitting potential decreased with increasing heat input. However even when the heat input was 12kJ/cm, the pitting potential was about 0.5V vs SCE and still higher than that of the 25%Cr duplex SS's base metal.

Next, the corrosion resistance of the tube-to-tube sheet weldment was investigated to evaluate the corrosion resistance of the seal weldment to be employed on the construction of a tubular heat exchanger. It is necessary before the testing to select a tube sheet material matching with the 28%Cr duplex SS tube. The corrosion of the tube sheet is in general thought to be less serious than the tube itself because the tube sheet is exposed to the lower temperature environment and the cathodic protection is more effeetively applied. For that reason the 25%Cr duplex SS plate was employed as the tube sheet material applicable to the 28%Cr duplex SS tube in this work. The edge preparation for welding was shown in Fig. 12. The welding was performed by GTAW with the heat input of 5.8kJ/cm using the 28%Cr or the 25%Cr duplex SS filler metal. The pitting potential was measured and the P. I. value of the weld metal was calculated based on the dilution of the weld metal by the tube and the tube sheet materials. context_after.text: 1) A super-duplex stainless steel which was composed of 27.5%Cr-7%Ni-3.8%Mo-0.3%N was developed from the investigation of the weldment performance. The seamless tube of the alloy was successfully manufactured by the powder metallurgical process.

2) The corrosion resistance of the 28%Cr duplex SS in hot seawater environments was superior to the conventional 25%Cr duplex SS and almost equal to those of super-ferritic and super-austenitic stainless steels.
